etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English correspondence, from Latin correspondentia. By surface analysis, correspond +‎ -ence.

definitions.definition: (uncountable) Reciprocal exchange of civilities, especially conversation between persons by means of letters.
(countable or uncountable) Postal or other written communications.

quote.citation: 1985 April 13, Michael Harmon, “Personal advertisement”, in Gay Community News, page 14:
quote.text: I'm doing time in Oklahoma and really would appreciate some correspondence.

definitions.definition: (countable) An agreement of situations or objects with an expected outcome.
(theology, Swedenborgianism) A similarity between physical and spiritual things (e.g. light to wisdom, or warmth to love)
Congruity or similarity between different things, people, etc:
